To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
acid soils are a major problem for agriculture in Australia and that genetics and biotechnology can help to solve this problem by increasing crop yields and improving soil health.
1. The yield losses associated with acid soils are large and will increase as soils become more acidic.

(i) Acid soils (pHA 5.0) limit the yields of Australian major crops and restrict the area that can be cropped; (ii) Acidification is caused by the leaching of base cations and the accumulation of toxic Al3+ and Mn2+; (iii) Acidification is exacerbated by agricultural practices, such as continuous cropping, that increase the rate of cation leaching; (iv) Liming has improved yields on acid soils but rates are too low
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of strategies to improve the yield of major grain crops on acidic soils.

the following questions. What are the genetic and physiological bases for acid soil tolerance in wheat, barley, lupin and chickpea? What is the potential for improving acid soil tolerance by pyramiding optimal alleles through breeding and by genetic engineering?

(i) the identification of genetic loci controlling acid soil tolerance, (ii) the development of a molecular marker system to facilitate the pyramiding of these loci in breeding lines, and (iii) the development of transgenic plants with improved acid soil tolerance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is potential for genetic gains in acid soil tolerance in all of Australia's major grains.
there is potential for genetics and biotechnology to increase the yield of major grain crops on Australian acid soils, but this potential is yet to be fully realised.
there are a range of genetic and biotechnological approaches to increasing yields on acid soils, but there are also many unknowns.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of genetics and biotechnologies to improve the yield of Australia’s major grain crops on acidic soils is a realistic prospect but the potential is not yet realised.
there is considerable scope for improving yields of wheat and barley on acid soils by breeding for tolerance to Al3+ toxicity and low pH.
acid soils pose various abiological stresses that limit the yields of Australian grain crops.
The main takeaway from our work is that
genetic improvement of crop varieties for acid soils will require a better understanding of the physiological processes that limit plant growth and yield.
genetic improvement of crops for acid soil tolerance is a viable option to maintain and increase yields in the short term.
genetic gains are possible and that the most effective strategy will be the pyramiding of the most effective loci for acid soil tolerance in a single genotype.
